primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: 11β-hydroxylase deficiency due to CYP11B1 loss of function
mechanism: CYP11B1 normally converts 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol and 11-deoxycorticosterone to corticosterone. Deficiency lowers cortisol, increases ACTH and adrenal androgen production, and causes accumulation of mineralocorticoid-active 11-deoxycorticosterone, leading to hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and suppressed renin.
vignette: A child has early virilization and rapid linear growth. Blood pressure is elevated, serum potassium is low, and plasma renin activity is suppressed. Cortisol is reduced and adrenal androgen concentrations are increased.
lead: Which enzymatic reaction is most likely impaired?
correct: Conversion of 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol and 11-deoxycorticosterone to corticosterone
distractors: Conversion of progesterone to 11-deoxycorticosterone and 17-hydroxyprogesterone to 11-deoxycortisol
distractor_notes: These are 21-hydroxylase reactions; 21-hydroxylase deficiency causes cortisol/mineralocorticoid deficiency and classically salt wasting rather than DOC-mediated hypertension.
17,20-lyase activity is part of CYP17A1; its deficiency reduces androgen production rather than causing androgen excess.
Aldosterone synthase deficiency impairs aldosterone production but does not cause the DOC and androgen excess of 11β-hydroxylase deficiency.
Cholesterol side-chain cleavage is the first step of all adrenal steroid synthesis; its failure would reduce mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids, and sex steroids broadly.
key_expl: 11β-hydroxylase, encoded by CYP11B1, catalyzes the terminal steps from 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol and from DOC to corticosterone. When the enzyme is deficient, cortisol falls and ACTH rises. Steroid flux is redirected toward androgens while DOC accumulates and acts as a mineralocorticoid, producing hypertension, hypokalemia, alkalosis, and low renin.
objective: Identify the blocked CYP11B1 reactions in 11β-hydroxylase deficiency and connect DOC accumulation with low-renin hypertension.
